Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

invent verb

also invention, inventor, inventive, think up, dream up, be invented, cook up

classical

Cic. Rep. 2.12: novam interrēgnī ineundī ratiōnem (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 15.82: nūper excōgitātum est
Traupman 296

excōgitō, excōgitāre, excōgitāvī, excōgitātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

invent, devise, think up

To find out by thinking: a plan, a method, a new thing. Lewis & Short: “frequent and classical”.

Other words

  • inveniō, invenīre, invēnī, inventum — find out, invent

    verb, fourth conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 3.3.35: quandam fallāciam (Lewis & Short); Cic. Dom. 1: multa dīvīnitus ā majōribus nostrīs inventa (Lewis & Short)

    Its plain sense is “find” (see find); “invent” is its figurative use. From it come inventor, inventōris m., an inventor (Aristaeus, quī olīvae dīcitur inventor, Cic. N.D. 3.45), and inventum, inventī n., an invention (Ov. Met. 1.521).

  • reperiō, reperīre, repperī, repertum — find out, discover, invent

    verb, fourth conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 8.246: serrae reperit ūsum (Lewis & Short); Quint. 2.17.4 (Lewis & Short)

    Its plain sense is “find” (see find); “invent” is its figurative use, frequent after Augustus (Lewis & Short): Ovid’s Perdix serrae reperit ūsum, invented the saw. An inventor is also repertor.

Examples

  • cum recentī fīcō salis vice cāseō vescī nūper excōgitātum est

    eating cheese with a fresh fig instead of salt is a recent inventionPlin. NH 15.82

  • Aristaeus, quī olīvae dīcitur inventor

    Aristaeus, who is said to have discovered the oliveCic. N.D. 3.45 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quis prīmus rotam excōgitāvit?

    Who invented the wheel?composed

See also find, develop, new, imagine.

Pliny from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-plinius); the other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
